sourceRules.rule: WorkingSetSize/WorkingSet64 represents pageable pages currently resident in physical memory for a process; it may include shared pages.
sourceRules.falsifier: Treat Working Set as Private Bytes, unique physical ownership or commit charge.
sourceRules.applicability: Windows API/counter semantics; target API availability is Runtime-only.

sourceRules.rule: PrivateUsage/Private Bytes is a process private commit-charge metric and is not interchangeable with current resident Working Set.
sourceRules.falsifier: Infer PrivateUsage from WorkingSet64 when the private counter is absent.
sourceRules.applicability: Exact PROCESS_MEMORY_COUNTERS_EX/API support and access are Runtime-only.

sourceRules.rule: System Available Physical Memory, Committed Bytes, Commit Limit and pagefile capacity describe distinct system-level quantities.
sourceRules.falsifier: Treat free RAM, commit charge and pagefile usage as the same metric.
sourceRules.applicability: Windows target build and counter/API availability required.

sourceRules.rule: PageFaultCount is cumulative and does not by itself provide a hard-page-fault rate; use appropriate system paging counters and workload evidence.
sourceRules.falsifier: Call cumulative PageFaultCount a hard-fault rate or performance bottleneck.
sourceRules.applicability: Counter semantics and collection interval are Runtime-specific.

sourceRules.rule: Cache/standby memory is normal Windows memory-manager behavior and is not default junk; do not clear or trim it without a specific measured workload reason and separate authority.
sourceRules.falsifier: Recommend indiscriminate standby-list clearing or working-set trimming as universal optimization.
sourceRules.applicability: OS version and workload behavior must be checked; server tuning thresholds are not universal client rules.

sourceRules.rule: A suspected leak requires repeated time-stamped measurements for a stable process instance under comparable workload, including idle/recovery behavior; a single sample is never leak proof.
sourceRules.falsifier: Label a high Working Set or one rising sample as a confirmed memory leak.
sourceRules.applicability: Stable process identity, workload comparator and sample availability are Runtime-only.

sourceRules.rule: An optimization improvement claim requires a comparable pre/post workload and a user-relevant response/throughput metric; increased available memory alone is insufficient.
sourceRules.falsifier: Claim speedup only from increased available bytes or reduced process Working Set.
sourceRules.applicability: Trusted workload comparator and outcome metric are Runtime evidence.

sourceRules.rule: Current Shun top-memory collector returns a bounded WorkingSet64 snapshot only; it does not establish process identity continuity, private commit, leak, cause or safe termination.
sourceRules.falsifier: Promote top-eight process rank to a process-control target or longitudinal diagnosis.
sourceRules.applicability: Exact Shun source commit is pinned; any later implementation change invalidates this rule.

decisionRules.action: Collect additional system/process metrics; explain signal only.

decisionRules.when: No LOW_FREE_MEMORY signal in current snapshot
decisionRules.action: Do not assert healthy/no-pressure; ask for workload or more evidence if slowness persists.

decisionRules.when: Only WorkingSet64 top-process facts are available
decisionRules.action: Show resident working-set ranking; do not infer private bytes, leak or cause.

decisionRules.when: Required metric/API/counter or stable identity is unavailable
decisionRules.action: Preserve field-level UNKNOWN; do not substitute another metric.
Provide safe review steps and explain evidence; no process/service/cache/pagefile/registry/hardware mutation.

decisionRules.when: Before/after evidence lacks trusted same-host/same-workload comparison and user outcome metric

runtimeOnly: before/after performance metrics and execution receipts
neverCompile: process lists, process names, PIDs, command lines, user names, environment or paths
host identifiers, user files or document contents
current permissions, approvals, grants, permits or Host identity
unverified LLM output, runtime evidence or execution receipts
invalidationTriggers: source Blob or source revision changes
Windows build, API or counter semantics change
PowerShell/provider implementation or output schema changes
new memory metric or changed units/collection semantics
Product, risk, privacy or authorization policy changes
SAP obligation, CQ, relation or Element ownership changes
promotionRule: No production AOT Package until fresh independent SAP qualification, Product admission where needed, DIS Function/ECP qualification, exact package digest and selected Runtime consumer proof are complete.
